checks.name: Companion radius
checks.detail: planet-sized

checks.name: Host type
checks.detail: a main-sequence dwarf (Teff 4857 K)

checks.name: Multiplicity
checks.detail: no sign of a companion in Gaia DR3 (astrometry, image shape, orbit and binary tables) or on ExoFOP
checks.value: Gaia DR3 RUWE 1.11, IPD harmonic 0.006, multi-peak 0% · ExoFOP companions 0

checks.name: Already catalogued
checks.detail: not a TOI, CTOI, known planet or catalogued binary at this period
checks.value: checked: TOIs, CTOIs, confirmed planets, TESS EB catalog, AAVSO VSX, Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries and orbits

checks.name: Period recovery
checks.detail: the dip is where the search put them, and 5.29 ppt deep there (found at 2.47 ppt): repeats are sought at that depth; no repeat of the transit in 350 days of TESS data (nothing of its depth above 7.0σ); most probable P ≈ 636 d (68%: 270-1270 d), from the periods the data allow and the transit probability; a second transit fixes it: the next TESS sectors of the star, or ground photometry
checks.value: 16 sectors scanned (350 d) · ZTF not used: 5.29 ppt is too shallow for its ~1-2% points · 22% of 10.8-2000 d allowed by the TESS coverage

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: one transit: the period is unknown
checks.value: BTJD 2190.26 (sector 32, TESS-SPOC): vetting SNR 16.6, 4.94 ppt (the search's SNR was 8.8: a different detrending, binning and noise estimate)

checks.name: Engineering data
checks.detail: no transit falls in a known engineering interval

checks.name: Raw flux (SAP)
checks.detail: the dip isn't significant against a local baseline in the pipeline flux either, so the raw flux can't confirm or rule it out
checks.value: 1 transit: pipeline flux 5.1 ppt ± 1.74, raw SAP 4.81 ppt ± 2.25 (expected 4.98 ppt after SPOC's crowding correction, CROWDSAP 0.98); s32 TESS-SPOC

checks.name: Background correlation
checks.detail: the dip doesn't follow the pipeline's background estimate
checks.value: raw SAP 4.81 ppt ± 2.25; with the background regressed out 4.74 ppt ± 2.26; flux-background correlation |r| 0.08 within ±1.5 d

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: compares transits with each other: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (single event)
checks.detail: a brightening at BTJD 3919.94 is also above the false-alarm threshold: the systematics make events this size in both directions
checks.value: the dip 19.1σ white, 16.7σ red (F_red 1.14 from 1533 box positions over 345 d); threshold 4.4σ (noise reaches it anywhere in that much data 1% of the time); strongest brightening 5.3σ red at BTJD 3919.94

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: how the SNR builds over transits: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: one transit: there's no period to check (the alias and shape checks bound it instead)

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: periods under 9.7 d would have shown a second transit in the data around the dip; on this star a 5.40 h transit needs P ≳ 58.9 d (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: survives 4 detrendings (two methods, transits masked) with the depth within 30%
checks.value: running median 0.5 d: 4.98 ppt (SNR 19.0); running median 1 d: 4.94 ppt (SNR 16.6); running median 2 d: 5.21 ppt (SNR 8.4); local quadratic 1.5 d: 5.04 ppt (SNR 13.9)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: one transit: nothing to compare its depth with (the pipeline and detrending checks test it instead)

checks.name: Odd/even depths
checks.detail: one transit: there are no alternate transits to compare

checks.name: Secondary eclipse
checks.detail: the deepest other dip (BTJD 3932.69) isn't in the raw flux once the background is accounted for: an artifact, not an eclipse; nothing else stands out
checks.value: deepest other dip: BTJD 3932.69, 2.15 ppt (6.1σ red); in raw SAP 0.0188 ppt ± 0.259, background regressed out -0.039 ppt; limit for an eclipse anywhere in 345 d of data: 0.942 ppt (3σ red)

checks.name: Transit shape
checks.detail: asymmetric: the second half is 53% deeper (5.1σ)
checks.value: T14 5.40 h, ingress 0.14 h (5% of the half-duration); depth 5.03 ppt

checks.name: Duration vs expected
checks.detail: with no period, the duration bounds it instead: P ≳ 58.9 d on this star (central, circular orbit)

checks.name: Period from the transit shape
checks.detail: ingress not resolved (SNR 16.6, ingress 0.14 h)

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: no variability above 0.5 ppt out of transit (smaller pulsations are handled by the pulsation test)
checks.value: no significant variability in 8 sectors

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: the transit survives subtracting the star's pulsations, at the same depth
checks.value: 4 periodic signals removed: 55.8 h (0.456 ppt), 76.5 h (0.358 ppt), 50.1 h (0.333 ppt), 32.7 h (0.308 ppt); transit 4.94 ppt (SNR 16.6) → 5.26 ppt (SNR 15.7), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities
checks.detail: the archival RVs allow K up to 27.9 km/s: even at the shortest allowed period (58.9 d) a stellar companion isn't excluded
checks.value: Gaia: 17 epochs, p(constant) 0.14, robust amplitude 25.2 km/s → K < 27.9 km/s

checks.name: Centroid shift
checks.detail: no significant centroid motion: the source is within ~76″ of the target (3σ)
checks.value: 2 sectors; implied source offset 18.1 ± 19.3″ (shift 0.0σ)

checks.name: Difference imaging
checks.detail: the source sits 18″ from the target where no catalogued star fits (Δχ² 91): an uncatalogued source, or a PSF mismatch
checks.value: s32: 1 transits, source 8.4σ; source 17.9 ± 2.5″ from the target

checks.name: Own pixel photometry
checks.detail: our own photometry of the pixels is too noisy here to confirm or rule out the dip
checks.value: s32: 5.22 ppt ± 2.46 with column-wise background, 5.12 ppt ± 2.43 without; pipeline 5.1 ppt ± 1.74 at the same transits (expected here ~4.08 ppt)

checks.name: Detector position
checks.detail: well inside the CCD
checks.value: no dead row or column in the cutout

checks.name: Aperture growth
checks.detail: too noisy in our own photometry to say whether the dip keeps its depth in a bigger aperture
checks.value: s32: r 1 px (3 px) -0.177 ppt ± 0.532, r 3 px (28 px) 5.15 ppt ± 2.09; expected in the large one from the neighbours' dilution -0.147 ppt

checks.name: Pointing jitter
checks.detail: no extra pointing jitter during the dip

checks.name: Aperture dependence
checks.detail: large/small depth ratio 2.70 (3.6σ). Not scored: QLP's 1x1 and 5x5 px apertures aren't dilution-corrected, and known on-target planets differ by up to 3x too; a pixel-level (TPF) test is needed
checks.value: small 1.21 ppt ± 0.3, large 3.28 ppt ± 0.481 (QLP, 1 sector)

checks.name: Nearby sources
checks.detail: 1 star within 1′ (3 TESS pixels) could make the dip and the pixel and centroid tests rule out the other 10: needs seeing-limited photometry of the neighbours on a transit night
checks.value: 13 of 56 Gaia DR3 stars within 2′ could cause a 4.94 ppt dip if eclipsed: Gaia 4762785514817815680 at 46″, T 17.7 (needs a 75% eclipse); Gaia 4762785892774935936 at 68″, T 14.0 (needs a 3% eclipse); Gaia 4762774103088635392 at 70″, T 17.1 (needs a 46% eclipse); Gaia 4762785720976245120 at 76″, T 15.4 (needs a 9% eclipse)

notes: Approximate re-implementation of TRICERATOPS (circular orbits, main-sequence companions, Sun-like hosts for background stars and for neighbours without a Gaia size); run TRICERATOPS/VESPA before claiming validation.
No high-resolution imaging: unresolved companions within ~1″ (65% of binaries at 184 pc) are allowed.
Archival RVs (K < 27.878107965580387 km/s) exclude 0% of target eclipsing-binary configurations.
No phase-0.5 data: secondary eclipses are unconstrained.
No odd/even depth measurement: twice-the-period binaries are only judged on shape.
Only the 12 most plausible of 13 viable neighbours were modelled.
Target scenarios assume the light curve is already corrected for neighbours' contaminating flux; eclipsing companions at other periods (x2P for bound/background stars) are not modelled.
